correctness.rationale: The independent parent and bond model is explicit, including which degree is original. Weighted-k subset measures admit a monotone inclusion coupling via elementary-symmetric log-concavity; fixed alternatives preserve coordinatewise root connectivity. Local covariance telescopes to the stated finite identity. A uniform upper bound forces every asymptotic maximizer into the bounded lambda=(1-p)log n window; the window limit has unique maximum at lambda=1. Rising-factorial moments yield the correlation constant. Endpoints and strictness are proved. Sixteen exhaustive finite rational models plus 294 recurrence comparisons passed, but do not replace the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The original root degree is a natural predictor of the percolated root-component size in a growing network. The theorem combines strict finite conditional order with a new explicit joint covariance and a sharp nontrivial near-critical optimizing scale and zeta constant; this is not a marginal re-expression or an arbitrary parameter slice. The vanishing fixed-p correlation offers a useful contrast to strong conditional ordering. It provides exact analytical benchmarks without claiming empirical prediction or a general theorem for other tree models.
